chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said:

People will pass through the Path (Sirat) in different ranks. The Path is thinner than a hair and sharper than the edge of a sword. Among them are those who pass like lightning, among them are those who pass like a galloping horse, among them are those who pass crawling, among them are those who pass walking, and among them are those who pass clinging to it, while the Fire seizes part of them and leaves part.

key_terms.الصراط: The Path/Sirat - the bridge spanning over Hellfire that all must cross
key_terms.طبقات: Ranks/levels - the different speeds at which people cross the bridge
key_terms.متعلقا: Clinging/hanging - the most precarious state of crossing, barely making it

ai.seo_question: What is the Sirat bridge in Shia Islam and how do people cross it?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the passage across the Sirat, the bridge over Hellfire that every person must cross on the Day of Judgment. People traverse it at speeds reflecting their faith and deeds: some pass like lightning, others like a galloping horse, some walk, some crawl, and some cling desperately as the Fire singes them. This hadith complements the Quranic statement that everyone will approach Hell (19:71), and reflects the Shia eschatological understanding that the Sirat is a real bridge whose crossing corresponds to one's spiritual state. The vivid hierarchy from lightning-fast to barely hanging on served as a powerful motivator for moral conduct in the audience.
